therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on metformin ≥1500 mg/day
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c (A1C) at Week 18

results.effect_size: Net mean difference in A1C: -1.02% (95% CI: -1.36 to -0.67)
biomarker_changes: FPG net mean difference: -25.5 mg/dL (95% CI: -37.7 to -13.3) at Week 18
2-hour postmeal glucose net mean difference: -54.1 mg/dL (95% CI: -74.7 to -33.6) at Week 18
A1C net mean difference at Week 30: -1.01% (95% CI: -1.40 to -0.62)
safety_signals: Serious adverse events occurred only in the placebo arm: myocardial ischaemia (n=1), upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage (n=1), upper limb fracture (n=1), adenocarcinoma pancreas (n=1), colon cancer (n=1), lymphoma (n=1)

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Metformin's suppression of hepatic glucose output complements sitagliptin's incretin-mediated insulin secretion, together producing greater glycemic control than either alone
modulation_entries.citation: Patients will receive blinded sitagliptin 100 mg q.d. and open-label metformin ≥ 1500 mg/day for up to 30 weeks
